rules.statement: Map a tenant's OpenID protocol endpoints, including the discovery document, under the tenant route, so that every endpoint, and `/.well-known/openid-configuration` in particular, is served beneath the tenant's issuer; never map them at absolute root routes when the tenant route is non-empty.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Discovery §4.3 requires the discovery document to be fetched from beneath the issuer. A path-based tenant strategy also cannot resolve the tenant when `{tenantId}` is missing from the matched route.
rules.check: Look for protocol endpoint groups mapped with an empty or hard-coded prefix while the issuer or base address includes a tenant path, and for endpoint routes that leave out the tenant route parameter.

rules.statement: Use a tenant's configured issuer as its base address exactly as configured, and never append the tenant route or any other request-derived path to it.
rules.why: The issuer is the tenant's complete identity and already names where the tenant is served. Appending to it creates doubled paths (e.g. `/acme/acme`) and makes the issuer depend on the request.
rules.check: Look for code that builds endpoint URLs or a base address by combining a configured issuer with the tenant route, the path base or other request data.

rules.statement: Validate at host startup that a statically configured issuer ends with its tenant route (a path base may come before it), and stop the host when it does not.
rules.why: An issuer that does not end with the tenant path would publish a discovery document from which nothing can be served, so the misconfiguration should fail fast.
rules.check: Look for static tenant or issuer configuration that is not checked at startup against the strategy's tenant route.

rules.statement: When binding a route template from the current request, pass the binder a new dictionary holding only that template's own parameters, never the request's live `RouteValueDictionary`.
rules.why: `TemplateBinder` consumes the values it binds and writes any leftovers as a query string. Passing the live values strips parameters from the request, which breaks links generated later, and can leak unrelated parameters into the URL.
rules.check: Look for `TemplateBinder.BindValues` (or similar binding APIs) called with `HttpContext.Request.RouteValues` or `GetRouteData().Values` directly instead of a filtered copy.

rules.statement: Generate absolute endpoint URLs with `LinkGenerator`, passing the request's route values as ambient values so that route-prefix parameters such as `{tenantId}` carry over, rather than supplying those prefix values explicitly at each link site.
rules.why: Ambient values are the routing system's own way to carry a route prefix's values. They only fill parameters of the target route and never become query parameters, while explicit values at each site would require every site to know the prefix.
rules.check: Look for link generation that leaves out ambient values (so prefix parameters are lost) or that manually adds tenant/prefix route values at individual call sites.

rules.statement: Leave out the scheme's default port when building the authority of a published URL, so that published URLs keep the issuer's own form (e.g. `https://op.example`, not `https://op.example:443`).
rules.why: An explicit default port makes published endpoint URLs differ from the issuer's form even though they name the same origin.
rules.check: Look for authority or URL construction that always writes the port (e.g. `Uri.Port` used unconditionally, or `UriBuilder` with an explicit port) instead of omitting it when `Uri.IsDefaultPort` is true.
